root_cause: Recomputable JSON and set digests did not bind persisted topic history to the literature snapshot used when it was saved. The global referenced-literature equality also treated legitimate preexisting inventory as an error before incremental reconciliation could run.

design.removed_invariant: Removed unconditional referenced-literature/global-literature set equality from topic state recovery.

authenticated_commitment.message: A domain-separated, length-prefixed concatenation of the exact persisted state bytes and canonical literature observation/artifact snapshot bytes.
authenticated_commitment.snapshot_contents: All LiteratureBase observation records and artifact metadata needed for integrity; artifact created_at is excluded as provenance-only so canonical dogfood replay remains stable.
authenticated_commitment.key_boundary: The 32-byte key is outside mutable JSON and is created atomically with restrictive mode 0600; the authentication sidecar is also written atomically with mode 0600.
authenticated_commitment.verification: Missing, malformed, replaced, mode-invalid, schema-invalid, digest-invalid, snapshot-mismatched, or MAC-invalid authentication state fails closed; MAC comparison uses hmac.compare_digest.

schema_and_recovery.legacy_behavior: Legacy state bytes are not migrated or rewritten on load and require explicit replay into a new state root.

design.literature_identity: LiteratureBase rejects persisted distinct observation IDs that reuse one idempotency key, while preserving valid idempotent replay of an existing observed record.

threat_boundary: This prevents data-path JSON or artifact writers that do not have signing authority from recomputing accepted history. It does not protect against a fully compromised same-user host or process that can read, replace, or use the signing key.
